subject: maths
title: Coordinates and Translations in the First Quadrant
seo_title: Year 4 Coordinates Worksheets: Plot Points, Translations and Shapes on a Grid
standard_text: Describe positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant; describe movements between positions as translations of a given unit to the left/right and up/down; plot specified points and draw sides to complete a given polygon.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 coordinates worksheets: read and plot coordinates in the first quadrant, describe translations left, right, up and down, complete squares and rectangles, and use maps and seating plans. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Along the corridor, then up the stairs: (x, y) means go along x, then up y.
key_sub: (3, 7) and (7, 3) are different points. In a translation, left and right change only x, and up and down change only y.
body_html:
What coordinates are

A coordinate grid has two axes. The x-axis goes across. The y-axis goes up. They meet at the origin, (0, 0).

Coordinates (x, y) tell you how to reach a point from the origin. Remember: along the corridor, then up the stairs. The first number is how far along. The second is how far up.

Example

A point is 6 squares along from the origin and 2 squares up. What are its coordinates?

Along 6 is the x-coordinate. Up 2 is the y-coordinate. Write the along number first.

Answer: (6, 2)

Order matters. (3, 5) and (5, 3) are different points. A point on the x-axis has y = 0, such as (4, 0). A point on the y-axis has x = 0, such as (0, 4).

Translations

A translation slides a point or shape without turning it. Moving left or right changes only x. Moving up or down changes only y.

MoveWhat changesExample from (5, 4)
right 2x gets bigger(7, 4)
left 2x gets smaller(3, 4)
up 2y gets bigger(5, 6)
down 2y gets smaller(5, 2)
Example

Describe the translation from (1, 6) to (4, 2).

Across: 1 to 4 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 squares down.

Answer: 3 squares right and 4 squares down

Completing a shape

To find the missing corner of a square or rectangle, line it up with the other corners. It shares its x-coordinate with one corner and its y-coordinate with another.

When a whole shape is translated, every corner moves the same way. Move each corner, then join them up.

Example

A triangle has corners at (1, 2), (4, 2) and (1, 6). It is translated 5 squares right. What are the new corners?

Add 5 to each x-coordinate. The y-coordinates stay the same.

Answer: (6, 2), (9, 2) and (6, 6)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping x and y: plotting (3, 7) at along 7, up 3Along the corridor first (x), then up the stairs (y)
Counting the lines, starting with 1 at the originThe origin is 0. Count the squares you jump
Moving the wrong way: adding for “left”Left and down make the number smaller
Changing only one coordinate for a move like “3 right, 2 up”Change x for left/right and y for up/down
Changing x for an up or down moveUp and down change only y

faq.q: What do children learn about coordinates in Year 4?
faq.a: In Year 4, children read and plot coordinates in the first quadrant, describe translations such as “3 squares left and 2 squares up”, and plot points to complete a shape. Reflections come in Year 5, and all four quadrants in Year 6.

faq.q: Which comes first in coordinates, x or y?
faq.a: The x-coordinate always comes first. Many teachers say “along the corridor, then up the stairs”: (4, 7) means along 4, then up 7.

faq.q: What is a translation in maths?
faq.a: A translation slides a point or shape left or right and up or down without turning it or changing its size. Moving left or right changes the x-coordinate, and moving up or down changes the y-coordinate.
It is the part of a coordinate grid to the right of the y-axis and above the x-axis, where both coordinates are 0 or more. Year 4 pupils work only in the first quadrant.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 3, then up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 6, then up 2. Point B is at (6, 2). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 2, then up 7. Point C is at (2, 7). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point P?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 8, then up 3. Point P is at (8, 3). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y). (3, 8) is point Q: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point F?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 1, then up 4. Point F is at (1, 4). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y). (4, 1) is point E: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 7, then up 6. Point G is at (7, 6). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 5, then up 9. Point H is at (5, 9). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y). (9, 5) is point J: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 4, then up 3. Point K is at (4, 3). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 9, then up 7. Point M is at (9, 7). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point R?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 6, then up 8. Point R is at (6, 8). Along the corridor (x) first, then up the stairs (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point S?
items.e: Point S is on the y-axis, so it does not go along at all: x = 0. It goes up 4. S is at (0, 4).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point V?
items.e: Point V is on the x-axis. Go along 6 and up 0: (6, 0). A point on the x-axis always has y = 0.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point W?
items.e: The x-coordinate tells you how far along to go. Point W is 7 squares along from the origin, so x = 7. (4 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point U?
items.e: The y-coordinate tells you how far up to go. Point U is 6 squares up, so y = 6. (3 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point Z?
items.e: Point Z is 8 squares along from the origin, so its x-coordinate is 8. Point Y is the one at (5, 8).

items.q: In coordinates such as (4, 7), which number comes first?
items.e: Coordinates are always written (x, y). Along the corridor, then up the stairs: the number for along comes first.

items.q: “Along the corridor, then up the stairs.” What does this help you remember?
c: Count the lines, not the squares
Start at the top of the grid
items.e: You walk along the corridor before you can go up the stairs. Go along the x-axis first, then up: (x, y).

items.q: In the coordinates (6, 2), what does the 2 tell you?
items.e: The second number is the y-coordinate. It tells you how far to go up: up 2. The 6 tells you to go along 6 first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of the origin, where the x-axis and y-axis meet?
items.e: The origin is the 0 on both axes. You have not moved along or up, so it is (0, 0).

items.q: Charlie starts at (0, 0). He goes along 4, then up 9. What are the coordinates of his point?
items.e: Along 4 gives x = 4 and up 9 gives y = 9. Write the along number first: (4, 9).

items.q: Which point is at (6, 2)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 6, then up 2: that is point B. Point A is at (2, 6): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (3, 7)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 3, then up 7: that is point C. Point A is at (7, 3): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (1, 5)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 1, then up 5: that is point D. Point A is at (5, 1): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (8, 4)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 8, then up 4: that is point A. Point B is at (4, 8): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (4, 9)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 4, then up 9: that is point B. Point A is at (9, 4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (7, 3)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 7, then up 3: that is point C. Point A is at (3, 7): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 6)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 2, then up 6: that is point D. Point A is at (6, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (5, 1)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 5, then up 1: that is point A. Point B is at (1, 5): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (9, 6)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 9, then up 6: that is point A. Point B is at (6, 9): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 8)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 2, then up 8: that is point D. Point A is at (8, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point has an x-coordinate of 5?
items.e: The x-coordinate is the first number: how far along. Point C is 5 squares along, at (5, 2). The point at (2, 5) has a y-coordinate of 5, not an x-coordinate of 5.

items.q: Which point has a y-coordinate of 3?
items.e: The y-coordinate is the second number: how far up. Point B is 3 squares up, at (6, 3). The point at (3, 6) has an x-coordinate of 3.

items.q: Aisha says point B is at (6, 3). What mistake did she make?
items.e: Point B is 3 squares along and 6 squares up, so it is at (3, 6). Aisha wrote the up number first.

items.q: Noah says point E is at (5, 3). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Point E is at (4, 2). Noah counted the line at 0 as 1, so both numbers came out 1 too big. Count the squares from the origin.

items.q: Are (2, 5) and (5, 2) the same point?
c: Yes, the order does not matter
Yes, they use the same numbers
items.e: (2, 5) is along 2, up 5. (5, 2) is along 5, up 2. The order of the numbers changes where the point is.

items.q: Zara wants to plot (7, 1). She goes up 7, then along 1. Which point did she plot by mistake?
items.e: Going along 1 and up 7 lands on (1, 7). To plot (7, 1), go along 7 first, then up 1.

items.q: Which point is further to the right: (2, 9) or (6, 1)?
items.e: How far right a point is depends on the x-coordinate, the first number. 6 is more than 2, so (6, 1) is further right.

items.q: Which point is higher on the grid: (8, 3) or (2, 5)?
items.e: How high a point is depends on the y-coordinate, the second number. 5 is more than 3, so (2, 5) is higher.

items.q: Which point is straight above (4, 2)?
items.e: Points straight above each other have the same x-coordinate. (4, 6) has x = 4, the same as (4, 2), and a bigger y.

items.q: Which point is straight to the right of (1, 5)?
items.e: Points straight across from each other have the same y-coordinate. (7, 5) has y = 5, the same as (1, 5), and a bigger x.

sets.title: Translations: left, right, up and down

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It is translated 2 squares right and 3 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 2 squares changes x: 3 + 2 = 5. Up 3 changes y: 4 + 3 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 3). It is translated 5 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays 2. Up 5 changes y: 3 + 5 = 8. The new point is (2, 8).

items.q: Point A is at (7, 5). It is translated 4 squares left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 4 squares changes x: 7 − 4 = 3. y stays 5. The new point is (3, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 6). It is translated 5 squares right and 3 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Down 3 changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (7, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (8, 3). It is translated 3 squares left and 4 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 3 squares changes x: 8 − 3 = 5. Up 4 changes y: 3 + 4 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (9, 8). It is translated 6 squares left and 5 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 6 squares changes x: 9 − 6 = 3. Down 5 changes y: 8 − 5 = 3. The new point is (3, 3).

items.q: Point P is translated 4 squares left and 1 square up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 4 squares changes x: 6 − 4 = 2. Up 1 changes y: 2 + 1 = 3. The new point is (2, 3). That is point D.

items.q: Point P is translated 3 squares right and 2 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 3 squares changes x: 1 + 3 = 4. Down 2 changes y: 6 − 2 = 4. The new point is (4, 4). That is point B.

items.q: Point P is translated 2 squares right and 4 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 2 squares changes x: 2 + 2 = 4. Up 4 changes y: 1 + 4 = 5. The new point is (4, 5). That is point A.

items.q: Point P is translated 2 squares left and 4 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 2 squares changes x: 7 − 2 = 5. Down 4 changes y: 7 − 4 = 3. The new point is (5, 3). That is point C.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 5). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 5 is 2 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (7, 2) and B is at (3, 2). Across: 7 to 3 is 4 squares left. The y-coordinate stays 2, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (1, 6) and B is at (4, 2). Across: 1 to 4 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 7) and B is at (2, 4). Across: 6 to 2 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 7 to 4 is 3 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (3, 1) and B is at (3, 7). The x-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 1 to 7 is 6 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A shape’s corner moves from (2, 7) to (8, 3). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (8, 3). Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A shape’s corner moves from (9, 1) to (5, 6). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (9, 1) and the end is at (5, 6). Across: 9 to 5 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point B is translated 3 squares right and 2 squares up. It lands on (7, 5). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards: undo each move. 3 right is undone by 3 left: 7 − 3 = 4. 2 up is undone by 2 down: 5 − 2 = 3. B started at (4, 3).

items.q: Arjun translates (5, 6) 3 squares left and gets (8, 6). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Moving left makes the x-coordinate smaller: 5 − 3 = 2. The correct answer is (2, 6). Arjun added 3, which is a move to the right.

items.q: A point is translated up or down. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: Up and down is the y direction. The point does not move left or right, so the x-coordinate stays the same.

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is straight in line with A up and down, so x = 1. It is straight in line with C across, so y = 5. D is at (1, 5).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a square. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is straight in line with C up and down, so x = 6. It is straight in line with A across, so y = 1. D is at (6, 1).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a square. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is straight in line with A up and down, so x = 3. It is straight in line with C across, so y = 6. D is at (3, 6).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 corners of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th corner, D?
items.e: D is straight in line with C up and down, so x = 4. It is straight in line with A across, so y = 1. D is at (4, 1).

items.q: The red dots are 3 corners of a square. Which point is the 4th corner?
items.e: The missing corner must line up with the red corners: x = 1 (straight above or below one corner) and y = 5 (straight across from another). That is (1, 5), point B.

items.q: The red dots are 3 corners of a rectangle. Which point is the 4th corner?
items.e: The missing corner must line up with the red corners: x = 8 (straight above or below one corner) and y = 2 (straight across from another). That is (8, 2), point A.

items.q: The red dots are 3 corners of a square. Which point is the 4th corner?
items.e: The missing corner must line up with the red corners: x = 7 (straight above or below one corner) and y = 5 (straight across from another). That is (7, 5), point C.

items.q: A rectangle has 3 corners at (1, 2), (6, 2) and (6, 5). What are the coordinates of the 4th corner?
items.e: The corners of a rectangle use just two x-coordinates (1 and 6) and two y-coordinates (2 and 5). The pair not used yet is (1, 5).

items.q: A square has 3 corners at (2, 3), (5, 3) and (5, 6). What are the coordinates of the 4th corner?
items.e: The corners of a square use just two x-coordinates (2 and 5) and two y-coordinates (3 and 6). The pair not used yet is (2, 6).

items.q: A rectangle has 3 corners at (0, 1), (0, 4) and (7, 4). What are the coordinates of the 4th corner?
items.e: The corners of a rectangle use just two x-coordinates (0 and 7) and two y-coordinates (1 and 4). The pair not used yet is (7, 1).

items.q: Plot these points and join them in order, then join the last point to the first: (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 4), (1, 4). Which shape do you make?
items.e: The sides are all 3 squares long and meet at right angles, so it is a square.

items.q: Plot these points and join them in order, then join the last point to the first: (2, 1), (8, 1), (8, 4), (2, 4). Which shape do you make?
items.e: The sides are 6, 3, 6 and 3 squares long and meet at right angles, so it is a rectangle.

items.q: Plot these points and join them in order, then join the last point to the first: (2, 2), (6, 2), (4, 6). Which shape do you make?
items.e: There are only 3 points, so joining them makes 3 sides: a triangle.

items.q: Plot these points and join them in order, then join the last point to the first: (1, 1), (7, 1), (5, 4), (3, 4). Which shape do you make?
items.e: The bottom side (y = 1) and the top side (y = 4) are parallel, but the other two sides slope. One pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Pick one corner and follow it. The bottom-left corner of A is at (1, 1). The bottom-left corner of B is at (5, 5). That is 4 squares right and 4 squares up. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Pick one corner and follow it. The bottom-left corner of A is at (6, 4). The bottom-left corner of B is at (2, 1). That is 4 squares left and 3 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: A triangle has corners at (1, 2), (4, 2) and (1, 6). It is translated 5 squares right and 1 square up. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (4, 2)?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 4 + 5 = 9. Up 1 changes y: 2 + 1 = 3. The new point is (9, 3). Every corner of the shape moves in the same way, so the shape stays the same size.

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (3, 5), (8, 5), (8, 9) and (3, 9). It is translated 2 squares left and 6 squares down. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (8, 9)?
items.e: Left 2 squares changes x: 8 − 2 = 6. Down 6 changes y: 9 − 6 = 3. The new point is (6, 3). Every corner of the shape moves in the same way, so the shape stays the same size.

items.q: A square has corners at (6, 1), (9, 1), (9, 4) and (6, 4). It is translated 4 squares left and 5 squares up. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (6, 4)?
items.e: Left 4 squares changes x: 6 − 4 = 2. Up 5 changes y: 4 + 5 = 9. The new point is (2, 9). Every corner of the shape moves in the same way, so the shape stays the same size.

items.q: A square has corners at (2, 2), (6, 2) and (6, 6). How many squares long is each side?
items.e: From (2, 2) to (6, 2) the y-coordinate stays 2, so subtract the x-coordinates: 6 − 2 = 4. Count the squares between the corners, not the lines (that gives 5).

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. What are the coordinates of the treasure?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 7, then up 6. The treasure is at (7, 6).

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. What is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Go along 2, then up 5: that is P, the palm tree. Always go along first: (5, 2) would be a different place.

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. Oliver starts at the palm tree. He walks 5 squares right and 1 square up. Where is he now?
items.e: The palm tree is at (2, 5). Right 5: 2 + 5 = 7. Up 1: 5 + 1 = 6. (7, 6) is the treasure.

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. Describe the move from the cave to the treasure.
items.e: The cave is at (5, 1) and the treasure is at (7, 6). Across: 5 to 7 is 2 squares right. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. A pirate walks along the grid lines from the well to the boat. What is the shortest number of steps?
items.e: The well is at (1, 2) and the boat is at (8, 2). They have the same y-coordinate, so walk straight across: 8 − 1 = 7 steps. Count the squares, not the lines.

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. A second treasure is buried 3 squares left of the treasure. What are its coordinates?
items.e: The treasure is at (7, 6). Left 3 changes only x: 7 − 3 = 4. y stays 6: (4, 6).

items.q: The map shows a treasure island. T = treasure, P = palm tree, C = cave, W = well, B = boat. Each square is 1 step. The boat sails 4 squares up. Where does it stop?
items.e: The boat is at (8, 2). Up 4 changes only y: 2 + 4 = 6. x stays 8: (8, 6).

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. What are the coordinates of the café?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go along 7, then up 2. The café is at (7, 2).

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. Which place is at (1, 6)?
items.e: Go along 1, then up 6: that is S, the slide.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. Alfie walks from the gate straight up to the fountain. How many steps does he walk?
items.e: The gate is at (4, 0) and the fountain is at (4, 4). Same x, so it is a straight line up: 4 − 0 = 4 steps.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. Describe the move from the fountain to the pond.
items.e: The fountain is at (4, 4) and the pond is at (7, 7). Across: 4 to 7 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 4 to 7 is 3 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. A bench is put 3 squares right and 1 square down from the slide. Where is the bench?
items.e: The slide is at (1, 6). Right 3: 1 + 3 = 4. Down 1: 6 − 1 = 5. The bench is at (4, 5).

items.q: The map shows a park. G = gate, F = fountain, P = pond, S = slide, C = café. Each square is 1 step. What is the shortest number of steps from the slide to the pond along the grid lines?
items.e: The slide is at (1, 6) and the pond is at (7, 7). Go 7 − 1 = 6 squares right and 7 − 6 = 1 square up. 6 + 1 = 7 steps.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. What are the coordinates of Freya’s desk?
items.e: Go along 5, then up 4. Freya sits at (5, 4). (4, 5) has the numbers swapped.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. Who sits at (1, 3)?
items.e: Go along 1, then up 3: that is M, Mohammed. Amelia is at (4, 1), and Oliver is at (1, 1).

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. Describe the move from Oliver’s desk to Amelia’s desk.
items.e: Oliver is at (1, 1) and Amelia is at (4, 1). Across: 1 to 4 is 3 squares right. The y-coordinate stays 1, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. Mohammed moves to a new desk 4 squares right and 2 squares up. Where is his new desk?
items.e: Mohammed is at (1, 3). Right 4: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 2: 3 + 2 = 5. His new desk is at (5, 5).

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. Describe the move from Mohammed’s desk to the teacher’s desk.
items.e: Mohammed is at (1, 3) and the teacher’s desk is at (3, 6). Across: 1 to 3 is 2 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 6 is 3 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some pupils sit. O = Oliver, A = Amelia, M = Mohammed, F = Freya, T = teacher’s desk. How many squares is it from Oliver’s desk straight up to Mohammed’s desk?
items.e: Oliver is at (1, 1) and Mohammed is at (1, 3). The x-coordinate stays 1, so subtract the y-coordinates: 3 − 1 = 2 squares.

items.q: In a computing lesson, Ethan’s robot starts at (1, 1). It moves 4 squares right, then 3 squares up, then 2 squares left. Where does it stop?
items.e: Follow one move at a time. Right 4: (5, 1). Up 3: (5, 4). Left 2: (3, 4). Left makes x smaller.
